newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Second wheat auction under new plan sees low sales.
newsitem.headline: Second wheat auction under new plan sees low sales.

text.p: The second auction of Brazilian wheat in a new scheme devised by the government to ensure farmers receive the minimum price resulted in the sale of only 4.60 percent of the wheat offered, a bank spokesman said.
Only 4,600 tonnes of the 100,000 tonnes included in today's auction was bought, said the spokesman from Banco do Brasil which held the electronic sale.
The first auction held on November 18 saw a similar result, with sales of only 4,600 tonnes.
The auction is designed to set not outright prices but the level of the subsidies to be paid by the government.
The buyer then pays the government the minimum price of 157 reais ($152.43) minus the subsidy while the government pays the farmer the full 157 reais.
Almost all of the wheat bought today was from Parana which accounted for 4,000 tonnes and which was bought for a subsidy of 25 reais ($24.27) for delivery in Rio de Janeiro and Espirito Santo states.
The remaining 600 tonnes was from Rio Grande do Sul for delivery in Sao Paulo state and fetched a subsidy of 24 reais.
-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
